name: Palms — curated world set
status: 5 archetypal species (full list archived in docs/plant_archive)
notes: The recognisable palms of every palm region: tropical coasts, oases, African savanna and swamp, Asian monsoon plains and rainforest, Australia and NZ, Andean cloud forest (the wax palm as an emergent), Amazon floodplain and swamp, the SE US, desert canyon oases, the Mediterranean, and cold-hardy hill palms. Tiers: emergent for the wax palm, canopy for trunked palms, shrub for trunkless and clumping palms, epiphyte for rattan (climbing). The 'palm' shape exists; Phase 6 should give it fan vs feather crowns, a clustering form, and the doum fork.

emergent.name: Andean wax palm
emergent.source: Palm of Colombian and Peruvian Andes cloud forest; height 40-60 m. Tallest palm on Earth; waxy white trunk above the cloud forest. Standard floras and Kew POWO for the name.

traits.native_range: Colombian and Peruvian Andes cloud forest
traits.leaf_shape: fan or feather fronds in a terminal crown
traits.trunk: single unbranched columnar trunk (doum forks; clumpers sucker)
traits.petiole: long fibrous petiole with a leaf sheath
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.notes: smooth waxy white to pale grey trunk with dark evenly spaced leaf-scar rings; wax coating makes it shine

leaf.notes: long pinnate fronds, dark green above, silvery-grey waxy beneath; leaflets drooping

flower.form: large branched cream inflorescences among the leaves

fruit.form: small round orange-red fruits 2 cm in big hanging bunches

appearance.silhouette: an impossibly tall thin white pole 40-60 m rising above the cloud forest with a small dark feather-duster crown
appearance.refs: Wikipedia Ceroxylon quindiuense; Kew POWO; Palmpedia

canopy.name: Coconut palm
canopy.source: Palm of tropical coasts worldwide; height 15-30 m. Leaning trunk, feather crown; sea-dispersed nuts. Standard floras and Kew POWO for the name.

bark.notes: grey-brown fibrous trunk with close ring scars; bulbous base; often curved

leaf.notes: long arching pinnate fronds with stiff glossy leaflets in one plane; yellow-green rachis

flower.form: creamy branched spadix from a boat-shaped spathe among the leaves

fruit.form: big three-sided nuts 25-35 cm, green to yellow-orange to brown, in clusters below the crown

appearance.silhouette: a leaning slender grey trunk with a loose spherical crown of 25-30 arching feather fronds; nuts clustered under it
appearance.refs: Wikipedia Cocos nucifera; Kew POWO; Palmpedia

bark.notes: trunk covered in persistent diamond-shaped leaf bases in a spiralling pattern, brown, fibrous between; base ringed with suckers

leaf.notes: stiff grey-green pinnate fronds with V-folded leaflets in several planes; lower leaflets become sharp spines

flower.form: cream-yellow branched spikes bursting from a spathe among the leaves

fruit.form: dates 3-7 cm, yellow to orange ripening amber-brown, in big hanging bunches on orange stalks

appearance.silhouette: a stout rough-scaled column with a full spherical crown of stiff grey-green fronds and hanging orange fruit bunches; suckers at the base; oasis groves

leaf.notes: huge costapalmate fan leaves 2-3 m across, deeply split into drooping segments, on long petioles; big rounded crown
